name: Patti Johnson
profile: Patti Johnson campaigned for SGA's finance-adjacent executive vice presidency in March 2003 on a platform that included support for one-stop billing, and won a contested election alongside Jessica Martin, who took the vice presidency of administration the same cycle. Johnson had already been active in SGA for several years before running, including committee work in public relations and athletics.

As executive vice president for 2003-04 she chaired Congress, the confirmed role at each of the four 2003-04 meetings checked on the record (2 September, 16 September and 2 December 2003, and 13 April 2004).

When Nick Todd, the officer elected president for 2004-05, resigned that July amid an investigation into missing SGA Dining Dollars funds, Johnson was the only student to come forward for the September 2004 special election, ran unopposed, and was sworn in as president on 23 September 2004 -- a full second term of SGA leadership, already documented at length in this archive's 2004-05 year record and not repeated here.

name: Nick Todd
profile: Nick Todd ran for SGA's finance office in the March 2003 election and was confirmed as vice president of finance at each of the four 2003-04 meetings checked on the record, reporting on the budget at the 2 and 16 September 2003 meetings. As finance vice president he had signing authority, along with outgoing president John Bradley and adviser Charley Pride, over the SGA Aramark Dining Dollars account, which opened the 2003-04 year with $5,000.

In March 2004 Todd ran for president against a fellow 2003-04 cabinet officer, vice president of administration Jessica Martin, and won with 772 of 1,232 votes cast. Days before the new officers were due to be sworn in, SGA's judicial council found $611 missing from the Dining Dollars account he had overseen as finance vice president; a senator drafted impeachment articles against the finance vice presidency he was about to leave, but the council ruled the two-week process could not finish before he left the post regardless. Todd publicly denied wrongdoing in the Herald's 22 April 2004 issue and was sworn in as president on 27 April 2004 with the investigation still unresolved.

Todd's subsequent 2004-05 presidency -- his resignation that July, the internal audit, and the September special election that followed -- is already documented in full in this archive's 2004-05 year record and is not repeated here.

name: Jessica Martin
profile: Jessica Martin ran for SGA's administration office in March 2003, campaigning on raising student awareness, and won the contested April 2003 election alongside Patti Johnson. She was confirmed as vice president of administration at each of the four 2003-04 meetings checked on the record, signing the minutes every time. This archive's 2004-05 record, drawing on SGA's own 2004-05 executive officer profiles, records her as having chaired the Academic Affairs committee and served as vice-chair of Constitutional Review earlier in her SGA career, though the sources do not pin those specific roles to the 2003-04 year itself.

In March 2004 Martin ran for president against fellow 2003-04 cabinet officer Nick Todd, the vice president of finance, arguing at a candidates' debate that unimplemented university programs could be frozen and savings spent while still available. She lost, 772 votes to 424.

After Todd's resignation that July and Katie Dawson's interim presidency, Martin remained active enough in SGA that fall to report application numbers for the vacant presidency and open senate seats at the September 2004 organizing meeting; when Patti Johnson won the special election, Martin became chief of staff under her, a role already documented in this archive's 2004-05 year record.

name: Abby Lovan
profile: Abby Lovan ran for SGA's public relations office in March 2003 and was confirmed as vice president of public relations at each of the four 2003-04 meetings checked on the record. This archive's 2004-05 record, citing SGA's own 2004-05 executive officer profiles, describes her as having been in SGA since her first semester at Western, working up through vice chair and then chair of the public relations committee, and chairing an ad hoc internal review committee -- though the sources do not specifically date those steps to the 2003-04 year rather than to earlier in her SGA career.

In March 2004 Lovan ran for one of the newly created senate's elected seats to continue her public relations work and received more votes than any other senate candidate on the ballot, 555. On 13 April 2004 she withdrew her name from the race for Speaker of the Senate, a post that instead went to Robert Watkins. She continued into 2004-05 as Director of Public Relations, the title her office took under the new constitution -- already documented in this archive's 2004-05 year record.

name: Skylar Jordan (also given as R. Skylar Jordan; 'Ricky Jordan' in some SGA records)
office: Justice, Judicial Council then Director of Academic and Student Affairs (2005-06); Director of Academic and Student Affairs (2006-07)
profile: 'Ricky Jordan' and 'Skylar Jordan' are the same person: data/name-aliases.json maps both 'Ricky Jordan' and 'R. Skylar Jordan' to 'Skylar Jordan', and the same person's own byline appears in the Herald as 'Skylar Jordan' as early as September 2005, while SGA records of the same period call him 'Ricky Jordan'. He was profiled as a candidate in the Herald's 15 March 2005 SGA-elections special section, then served as Justice of the Judicial Council for 2005-06 (per the year's confirmed organization record) and wrote a Herald opinion piece, 'The Tearing Down of Snell Hall Is Tragic,' that September.

He was appointed mid-year to Director of Academic and Student Affairs, succeeding Katie Pettit in that post; Senator Willie Cravens questioned the appointment at the 7 March 2006 Senate meeting, and Jordan was confirmed reporting to the Senate in the role by the 4 April 2006 meeting used as this project's anchor. He continued as Director of Academic and Student Affairs into 2006-07.

He remained in SGA's cabinet at least two years further, as Chief of Staff for 2007-08 and again for 2008-09, per the organization records already in data/years.json for those years -- continuity this draft flags but does not re-research, since it falls outside 2005-06/2006-07. During his time as Chief of Staff, the Herald reported on 8 April 2008 that he filed a complaint with SGA's judicial council against something called the 'Red Towel Party'; a follow-up Herald report on 22 April 2008 says the council decided to take no action on the complaint. Neither article's body text was reachable to establish what the Red Towel Party was or the substance of the complaint beyond the headlines. He returned to SGA as a guest speaker addressing the Student Senate on 22 February 2010, per that meeting's minutes -- by then an alumnus of the cabinet.

name: Kendrick Bryan
profile: Kendrick Bryan was already writing Herald guest columns as an SGA member before he became an officer -- on music downloads (April 2008) and a smoke-free-campus policy (February 2009) -- and continued writing columns about SGA and student involvement in his own voice through the whole span of his eventual three consecutive years as executive vice president: 2009-10 (this project's original anchor, both the SGA site's archived executive-branch page and Herald election coverage), 2010-11, and 2011-12.

In the March 2010 election for the 2010-11 term he ran against Currie Martin for executive vice president, and the Herald's editorial board endorsed him alongside presidential candidate Colton Jessie (both won). During 2010-11 he was quoted defending the Greek community's roughly 40 percent share of SGA's fifty members as a strength rather than a problem (Herald, 11 Feb 2011) and championed a bill donating 30 Praxis Series teacher-certification test-prep books, bought for $495 through a partnership with the WKU Store, to the new Educational Resources Center in Gary Ransdell Hall (Herald, 15 Feb 2011). SGA's Secretary of the Senate recorded him giving a routine executive report at the 22 February 2010 meeting -- rallying attendance for a fair-housing rally, pushing for wifi in graduate housing, and meeting with Academic Affairs on scholar development.

He ran for a third term in the March 2011 election for 2011-12 and won it uncontested after opponent Katie Stillwell withdrew (Herald, 12 Apr 2011). That fall the Herald reported he had personally created a test-prep website (Herald, 6 Sep 2011, headline only -- body unreachable), and he was credited alongside President Billy Stephens with originating the idea of lending Educational Resource Center iPads loaded with study material to students free of charge (Herald, 30 Sep 2011). He did not seek a fourth term in March 2012; the Herald quoted him that month, as outgoing executive vice president, describing how Keyana Boka -- who had worked closely with him on campus-improvements projects -- had approached him about running to succeed him, and he supported her candidacy (Herald, 23 Mar 2012). Boka went on to win the office unopposed for 2012-13.
